correctness.rationale: For every a>=8, the coin cost for {1,3,7} is derived by exhaustive residue arithmetic in t modulo three; an exact Apéry formula follows from comparing representatives M=m+qa, with no unseen smaller residue representatives. The Apéry-order argument proves maximality is equivalent to absence of cost-one coin extensions; only final seven indices need evaluation and all seven residues are enumerated. Standard Apéry pseudo-Frobenius correspondence proves the complete infinite claim. Independent Dijkstra shortest-path Apéry and direct gap DP tests on exact specified ranges corroborate, rather than replace, the universal proof.
